newsitem.title: HAITI: Haiti seeks funds allegedly stolen by Duvaliers.
newsitem.headline: Haiti seeks funds allegedly stolen by Duvaliers.

text.p: The Haitian government has filed a legal complaint against 35 people allied with former President Jean-Claude Duvalier, alleging that they pillaged the Haitian Treasury, government attorneys said on Tuesday.

The complaint, filed in Port-au-Prince court at the end of January, represents the latest attempt to retrieve money widely believed to have been stolen by Duvalier's followers when they left the country.
It named the ex-president's mother, Simone Duvalier, his sisters Marie Denise and Simone Duvalier, his ex-wife Michele Bennet and her father Ernest Bennet, and former members of Duvalier's cabinet.
The complaint accused them of "embezzlement of funds, theft, pillaging public funds and damage to the Haitian state."

Duvalier, most of his family and many supporters were forced into exile in 1987 by a popular uprising that eventually led to the election of Jean-Bertrand Aristide, the nation's first freely elected president.
Duvalier headed a repressive regime that he inherited from his father, Francois "Papa Doc" Duvalier. The two ruled Haiti, the poorest nation in the western hemisphere, for 30 years.
Jean-Claude Duvalier reportedly still lives in France, but members of his family and his former father-in-law have returned to Haiti.

The complaint, compiled from a 1988 report by Haiti's general accounting office, represents the first attempt to target Duvalierists outside of Duvalier's direct family, said Ira Kurzban, a U.S. lawyer representing the Haitian government.
Altogether, the government estimates that some $500 million was stolen by the Duvalier regime, Kurzban said, who led a successful legal campaign to win a judgment against Duvalier's ex-wife.
"We've already won an $11 million judgment against her," Kurzban said.
About $300,000 was retrieved from one of Michele Bennet's bank accounts and a seizure is in progress of a $450,000 apartment she owns on the Upper East Side of Manhattan.
